scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: The ground feels solid, until suddenly it shakes. What makes the Earth move under our feet?

scenes.name: plates
scenes.text: Earth's outer shell is broken into giant tectonic plates, which slowly move, a few centimetres a year.

scenes.name: stuck
scenes.text: Where plates meet, along faults, the rocks get stuck by friction, while the plates keep pushing.

scenes.name: stress
scenes.text: Stress builds up for years, bending the rock like a stretched spring.

scenes.name: slip
scenes.text: When it's too much, the rock suddenly slips, releasing energy as seismic waves.

scenes.name: waves
scenes.text: Faster P waves arrive first, then stronger S and surface waves cause most of the shaking.

scenes.name: measure
scenes.text: Seismometers record the waves, and magnitude is measured on a scale where each step is about thirty two times more energy.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Plates push, rocks stick, then slip and shake. Follow for more on how things really work.
